fixes.explanation: True, baker. Jesus says, “Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.” Every day, and still no arrest until now.
He runs, baker. They caught hold of him, but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked. The cloth stayed behind and he kept going.
They're not gone. Jesus comes back and finds Peter, James and John sleeping. Running off comes later in the passage, so hold on to that.

True, and it's a kind thing to say to sleepy friends. Jesus says, “For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.” He says it right after telling them, “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.” He names it plainly.
It's true, and Jesus says it Himself. His words are, “For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.” He says it after finding them sleeping.
No promises are recorded here. The text says they did not know what to answer Him. I think when you've just been caught napping, a promise is a lot to come up with.
They don't offer that excuse. The text says they did not know what to answer Him. Nobody tries to explain it away.
Yes, His betrayer. Jesus says, “Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!” He tells them to rise and then points out who is coming.
That's not who Jesus names. He says, “See, My betrayer is approaching!” The one coming is the person who will hand Him over.

Spears and shields would look impressive, but the verse doesn't list them. What the crowd carries is swords and clubs. Judas arrives with them, and they were sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
Bows and arrows don't show up here. The text puts swords and clubs in the crowd's hands. The men who sent them were the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
That's the reason He gives. Jesus says, “But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.” So what's unfolding here isn't random.
It's the opposite, friend. The text says, “Then everyone deserted Him and fled.” That's a heavy moment, so I think it's worth sitting with.
No fighting from him. They caught hold of the young man, but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away. He left with nothing but himself.
